record.paper_title: Open questions in descriptive set theory and dynamical systems
record.original_question: For all minimal subshifts, is topological conjugacy hyperfinite, or is it instead a universal countable Borel equivalence relation?

evidence.quote: Question 1.8 (Gao). Is the topological conjugacy relation for all minimal subshifts hyperfinite or a universal countable Borel equivalence relation?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. Let $A$ be a finite alphabet with the discrete topology, and let $A^{\mathbb{Z}}$ be the space of bi-infinite sequences over $A$ with the product topology, on which the shift map $\sigma:A^{\mathbb{Z}}\to A^{\mathbb{Z}}$, $\sigma(x)(n)=x(n+1)$, acts as a homeomorphism. A subshift is a nonempty closed subset $X\subseteq A^{\mathbb{Z}}$ with $\sigma(X)=X$. A subshift $X$ is called minimal if it has no proper nonempty closed shift-invariant subset; equivalently, every $\sigma$-orbit in $X$ is dense in $X$. Two subshifts $(X,\sigma)$ and $(Y,\sigma)$ (possibly over different finite alphabets) are topologically conjugate if there exists a homeomorphism $h:X\to Y$ with $h\circ\sigma=\sigma\circ h$.

Fix a way of coding minimal subshifts (over varying finite alphabets) as elements of a standard Borel space $\mathcal{M}$ — for example, by coding each minimal subshift via its language, viewed as a closed subset of $\bigcup_{k\geq 1}\bigcup_{n\geq 1}\{1,\dots,k\}^n$. Let $E_{\mathrm{conj}}$ be the equivalence relation on $\mathcal{M}$ given by topological conjugacy. Then $E_{\mathrm{conj}}$ is a countable Borel equivalence relation.

Recall that a countable Borel equivalence relation $E$ on a standard Borel space $X$ is hyperfinite if $E=\bigcup_n F_n$ where $F_0\subseteq F_1\subseteq\cdots$ is an increasing sequence of Borel equivalence relations each having finite classes. A countable Borel equivalence relation $E_\infty$ is universal if every countable Borel equivalence relation $F$ Borel reduces to $E_\infty$, i.e., there is a Borel map $f$ with $x\,F\,y\iff f(x)\,E_\infty\,f(y)$.

Question. Is $E_{\mathrm{conj}}$ hyperfinite, or is it a universal countable Borel equivalence relation?
artifact.category_tag: Descriptive set theory; countable Borel equivalence relations
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears still open. Recent works establish hyperfiniteness only for restricted subclasses (e.g., Toeplitz subshifts with separated holes, generalized Oxtoby subshifts), and surveys explicitly state that for minimal subshifts in general the conjugacy relation is known to be non-smooth but it is not known whether it is hyperfinite or universal.

status_evidence.title: Generalized Oxtoby subshifts and hyperfiniteness
status_evidence.snippet: The conjugacy relation for minimal symbolic subshifts is not smooth but it is not known whether it is hyperfinite or not.
status_evidence.claim: Status of conjugacy of minimal subshifts as a countable Borel equivalence relation is open.

status_evidence.title: On the complexity of topological conjugacy of Toeplitz subshifts
status_evidence.snippet: Topological conjugacy of Toeplitz subshifts with separated holes is hyperfinite.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress: hyperfiniteness has been established for certain subclasses of minimal subshifts.

status_evidence.title: Orbit equivalence of Cantor minimal systems
status_evidence.snippet: Studies of orbit equivalence and conjugacy for Cantor minimal systems within the descriptive set-theoretic framework.
status_evidence.claim: Active research area; full classification of minimal-subshift conjugacy as hyperfinite vs universal is not yet resolved.
